This page replaces the CNI of a node with Cilium. It shows what to put in the
cloud-config, how to make sure that the install worked, and what changes if you
also remove kube-proxy. Corium ships kube-router because k0s ships it. That one
component does networking, network policy and service proxying. To replace it,
you make two decisions.

> This page applies to a node that you are about to boot, not to a cluster that
> already runs. Corium renders `cni: custom` into `/etc/k0s/k0s.yaml` at
> bootstrap. To change it later, you must edit that file and restart k0s.

For a single node, start at [Configure the node](#configure-the-node).
For multiple nodes, read [Multi-node clusters](#multi-node-clusters) first.
The CNI is a decision for the whole cluster, and you must declare the chart on
the controller only.

Both decisions go in the cloud-config that the node already boots with. First,
k0s must install no CNI, so that two CNIs do not conflict on the same node.
Second, something must install Cilium. `cni: custom` does the first, and an
entry under `addons:` does the second. The node then gets to the correct state
without help, and you do not need a second provisioning step.

## Configure the node

```yaml
#cloud-config
corium:
  role: single

  network:
    podCIDR: 10.244.0.0/16
    cni: custom

  addons:
    - name: cilium
      chart: cilium/cilium
      version: 1.20.2
      namespace: kube-system
      repository:
        name: cilium
        url: https://helm.cilium.io/
      values:
        ipam:
          mode: cluster-pool
          operator:
            clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList:
              - 10.244.0.0/16
```

This is a complete node. [`examples/custom-cni.yaml`](https://github.com/Corium-OS/Corium/blob/main/docs/examples/custom-cni.yaml)
is the same document with an SSH key, ready to boot.

Before you boot anything, validate the document:

```bash
corium-agent validate node.yaml
node.yaml: valid (role single, cluster corium)
```

## What `cni: custom` and `addons:` do

`cni: custom` renders `spec.network.provider: custom` into `/etc/k0s/k0s.yaml`.
k0s then deploys no CNI. The node registers, comes up `NotReady`, and stays
`NotReady` until Cilium runs. This state is expected, and it is not a failed
boot. See [troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) to tell the two apart.

`addons:` renders `spec.extensions.helm`. k0s turns this into `Chart` resources
that its own controller reconciles, with no Helm binary and no in-cluster
operator. The controller runs the install, not a pod. So the install works while
the cluster has no pod network yet, and this is why you can install a CNI this
way. The Cilium agent and operator both run on the host network, so they do not
need the network that they will provide.

`corium-agent bootstrap --dry-run` shows what the two fields produce, and it
does not change the machine. The output below shows only the parts that this
page is about:

```yaml
# /etc/k0s/k0s.yaml
spec:
    extensions:
        helm:
            charts:
                - chartname: cilium/cilium
                  name: cilium
                  namespace: kube-system
                  values: |
                    ipam:
                        mode: cluster-pool
                        operator:
                            clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList:
                                - 10.244.0.0/16
                  version: 1.20.2
            repositories:
                - name: cilium
                  url: https://helm.cilium.io/
    network:
        podCIDR: 10.244.0.0/16
        provider: custom
        serviceCIDR: 10.96.0.0/12
```

Corium passes the chart values through without changes. It does not compare
them with the rest of the configuration. You must make sure that
`clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList` agrees with `network.podCIDR`. If they disagree,
pods get addresses that the cluster does not route.

## Nothing to configure for the immutable filesystem

On a read-only OS, two items usually need work. Corium already handles both:

- `/opt/cni/bin` is writable. The image points `/opt` at `/var/opt`, because
  the CNI DaemonSet installs its binary there. Without this, the first error
  you see is `mkdir /opt/cni:
  read-only file system`. The chart defaults, `/opt/cni/bin` and
  `/etc/cni/net.d`, are already where k0s looks. You do not need to set
  `cni.binPath` and `cni.confPath`.
- The inotify limits are higher. On a stock host, `cilium connectivity test`
  fails with *too many open files*. The image ships the higher values in
  `/usr/lib/sysctl.d/`.

## Verify the install

```bash
k0s kubectl get charts -A                                 # did the chart install
k0s kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=cilium     # is the agent running
k0s kubectl get nodes                                     # Ready, once it is
```

A few minutes after boot, all three of these must be true:

- `get charts -A` lists `k0s-addon-chart-cilium` in `kube-system`. If it is
  missing, k0s did not see the add-on. Make sure that the `addons:` block is
  correct.
- The Cilium agent pod is `Running` and `1/1` ready, one per node. `Pending`
  means that nothing scheduled it. `CrashLoopBackOff` means that it started and
  failed, so read its logs.
- The node is `Ready`, approximately one minute after the agent reports healthy.
  Until then, `NotReady` is expected, because nothing installed a network yet.

If you install the [Cilium CLI](https://github.com/cilium/cilium-cli/releases),
`cilium status --wait` gives more information.

## Without kube-proxy

Cilium can do all of the service handling. This needs two changes, and both
must be in the configuration that the node first boots with. To remove
kube-proxy from a cluster that already runs it is a different task, and a more
difficult one.

```yaml
corium:
  role: controller+worker

  cluster:
    endpoint: 10.0.0.10

  network:
    cni: custom

  # kube-proxy has no corium: key. k0s.patch is applied verbatim to the
  # rendered k0s.yaml, so every k0s setting stays reachable.
  k0s:
    patch:
      spec:
        network:
          kubeProxy:
            disabled: true

  addons:
    - name: cilium
      chart: cilium/cilium
      version: 1.20.2
      namespace: kube-system
      repository:
        name: cilium
        url: https://helm.cilium.io/
      values:
        kubeProxyReplacement: true
        k8sServiceHost: 10.0.0.10
        k8sServicePort: 6443
```

Here, `k8sServiceHost` is required. Cilium must reach the API server to load its
own configuration. Usually it uses the in-cluster `kubernetes` Service, but that
Service is a ClusterIP, and nothing translates it yet. kube-proxy is gone, and
Cilium is its replacement. Give Cilium an address that works without a cluster
network: the address of a controller, or the HA virtual IP.

## Multi-node clusters

The CNI is a decision for the whole cluster, and the control plane makes it:

- Declare the chart on the controller only. If a worker declares `addons:`,
  validation rejects it with `addons: only a controller installs add-ons, but
  role is "worker"`. The worker does not ignore it without a message.
- Put `network:` on the controller too. Corium writes the k0s cluster
  configuration on controllers only, so it never renders the `cni:` value of a
  worker.
- Workers need nothing. A worker that joins later is `NotReady` until the
  DaemonSet starts on it, then `Ready`. There is no step for each node.

## Troubleshooting

The node is `NotReady` and there are no Cilium pods. The chart did not install.
`k0s kubectl get charts -A` shows what k0s thinks it did, and
`journalctl -u k0scontroller | grep -i helm` tells you why it did not. The usual
cause is a version that does not exist. The second cause is a node with no route
to `helm.cilium.io`, because k0s fetches the repository at install time.

Cilium crash-loops with `Unable to contact k8s api-server`. With
`kubeProxyReplacement: true`, the cause is a missing or wrong `k8sServiceHost`.
The agent tries to reach the API server through a Service IP that nothing
translates.

Pods get addresses that the cluster does not route.
`clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList` and `network.podCIDR` disagree. Nothing makes sure
that they agree, so you must do it.

Everything works, but you expected kube-router. `cni: custom` stays after
bootstrap. Corium renders it into `/etc/k0s/k0s.yaml` at bootstrap. To change it
later, edit that file and restart k0s. A reboot does not change it.

## Other CNIs

Only the values on this page are specific to Cilium. You install any CNI that
comes as a chart with `cni: custom` and an add-on. Look for the same two
failures: a chart that does not install, and a pod CIDR that disagrees. Calico
is the exception. It has its own value, `cni: calico`, and k0s installs it for
you.

The [configuration reference](/docs/reference/configuration/#34-network) describes every field on
this page. [Feature support](/docs/reference/feature-support/#passthrough) lists what else
`k0s.patch` can reach.
